anomaly: 3 of the last 4 jobs failed inspection (jobs 1, 2, 4)
conclusion: The failures are not explained by a CNC-05-specific fault. Jobs 1 and 2 ran on CNC-05 and failed, job 3 ran on CNC-04 and passed, and job 4 ran on CNC-03 and failed, so a cause limited to CNC-05 cannot account for the job-4 failure on CNC-03 (E3, E18). Machine-specific checks rule out the main CNC-05 failure modes: CNC-05 hydraulic pressure is very steady (~68–71, no instability across failed-job vs passed-job windows, E20); CNC-05 following error is not higher than CNC-01's (CNC-01 means are comparable or higher, e.g. 4.995 vs 3.746 in ticks 360–389, E15 vs E17); CNC-05 vibration is stable (E19); and CNC-05 speed is essentially standard at 902 rpm (E6). The pattern is most consistent with a common or line-level cause—incoming material lot variation, inspection-station inconsistency, or shared tooling—rather than one machine. Confidence is moderate (~0.55), below the 0.90 needed to authorize an intervention, and none of the approved machine actions (bearing replacement, speed reset, servo drive, hydraulics repair) would fix a material/inspection common cause. Evidence that would raise confidence: material certificates/receiving inspection for the lots used in jobs 1, 2 and 4 versus job 3, an inspection-station repeatability check, and dimensional checks on rejected parts to see whether job 4 shares the same material lot as jobs 1 and 2.

anomaly: alarm on CNC-03: vibration 5.12 mm/s above 4.50
conclusion: CNC-03 showed a transient vibration spike of ~5 mm/s (above the 4.50 mm/s threshold) during ticks 71-78 while the machine was idle with near-zero load (load ~0-3%) and stable temperature (~68-74°F). The vibration then fell back below threshold by ticks 79-80 (0.37 and 0.17 mm/s). The other running machines, CNC-01 and CNC-02, showed normal vibration around 2-2.6 mm/s with no simultaneous factory-wide disturbance, so this is not a mechanical failure or external coupled disturbance — it is a transient CNC-03 vibration-sensor/instrument disturbance. CNC-03 is currently idle and no production impact is ongoing.
